action: If you took part in the second Modu-ui Changeop program, expect smishing and phishing messages using your name and phone number; do not follow links or give codes. Organisations: check what personal data your AI vendors hold.
exec: A supplier to a government startup programme was breached for the second time this year, showing that vendor security controls in public programmes are not holding.
impact: Data on 20,028 users exposed, including 818 programme participants.
plain: A Korean AI company that supports a government startup programme was hacked. Names, phone numbers and emails of about 20,000 users, including 818 programme participants, were exposed.
summary: Korea's Ministry of SMEs and Startups said on 13 November that AI provider Amicus Rex detected an external hacking attempt on 11 November. Personal data of 20,028 users was exposed, including 818 participants of the second Modu-ui Changeop programme: names, phone numbers and email addresses. The report notes a similar breach in June at the first programme.
title: Korean startup-programme supplier Amicus Rex hacked; 818 participants' contact data exposed

validation.note: One press report relaying the ministry announcement.

date_note: Detected on 11 November; the ministry announced it on 13 November (Yonhap, published 13 November).

review.note: Yonhap reprint (13 Nov) matches: detection 11 Nov 8:30, 20,028 users, 818 participants, name/phone/email, June precedent; added missing date_note. Note: the 818 figure is headlined as signs of leakage
